all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] The bare-layout test drives a single linked worktree only; no second worktree reads the shared store, and the removed-worktree case is not covered. A regression in cross-worktree store sharing or removed-worktree reporting in a bare layout would not be caught.

confirmed.desc: [ADVISORY] The bare-layout test drives a single linked worktree only; no second worktree reads the shared store, and the removed-worktree case is not covered. A regression in cross-worktree store sharing or removed-worktree reporting in a bare layout would not be caught.

rejected.desc: [BUG] With a bare main worktree RunStoreRoot falls back to RootOr(start), the linked worktree status runs in, so discoverAbandonedRuns' unattributable-run rule (here == main) is true in every worktree and an abandoned run whose worktree was removed becomes a MustClear blocker in all of them. In the bare+worktrees layout #174 enables, removing a worktree that left an FSM run at a non-terminal node makes status exit 1 and the Stop hook block in every other worktree, and the run cannot be advanced because its work dir is gone.

[ADVISORY] In a bare layout the anchor (RepoRoot) is whichever linked worktree runs the command, but the storeRoot block comment and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md still say the anchor is the main worktree. Readers are told the anchor is always the main worktree; per-worktree anchors surprise them.

findings.consequence: A transient git failure lets the Stop hook pass over a live worktree's abandoned run in a bare layout.
findings.issue: owner() returns unattributable both when the run's worktree is gone and when StoreDir/Toplevel fail transiently on a live worktree; with a bare main that run is orphaned (warning) instead of a blocker.

findings.consequence: Rarely, the warning names a nonexistent path.
findings.issue: The orphan warning always names <StoreDir>/runs/<id>, but an orphan can come from the 0.13.x legacy source.
